title: Errors, logs and booking metrics
idea: Good error handling throws typed exceptions with stable codes from the core, then catches them at one boundary that logs once, counts the outcome and answers the caller.
points: `BookingService` throws and never logs; the boundary decides what a failure means.
A rejected booking is a normal outcome: log WARN with code and context.
Unknown ids get WARN and 404; other exceptions are bugs: ERROR and 500.
Count every outcome by code; alert on the error rate, not on rejections.

steps.caption: A clash makes `BookingService` throw `RoomTakenException`. It adds no log line of its own.
`BookingEndpoint` catches the `BookingException` family first and reads its stable `code()`.
It writes one WARN line with the code, employee, room and slot, so support can search it.
It bumps a counter named after the code and maps the code to a status for the caller.
A null id is a defect, not a rule. It falls through to the last catch: ERROR and 500.
Dashboards watch `booking.error`. A rise there pages someone; more rejections only mean busy rooms.

code.title: The problem
code.caption: A catch-all turns a busy room and a null bug into the same false, logged twice as ERROR.

walk.text: `book` returns a boolean, so the reason for a failure has nowhere to go.
A clash throws a generic exception just to reach the shared catch below.
`catch (Exception e)` also swallows the `NullPointerException`. The bug is hidden, not handled.
The endpoint logs again and answers 500 for both cases. On-call is paged for a busy room.
Compare the second and third outputs: identical, though one is a user conflict and one a defect.

code.title: The fix
code.caption: Typed exceptions from the core, one boundary that logs once, maps codes and counts outcomes.

walk.text: `BookingException` is unchecked and abstract; each subclass returns a fixed `code()` clients can rely on.
The trimmed service only throws. It knows nothing about logs, metrics or HTTP.
Context is built once. Success logs INFO with the new id and counts `booking.created`.
Business rejections log WARN, count per code, and map to 400, 403 or 409 with a switch.
An unknown id is the caller's mistake: WARN and 404. Anything else is a defect: ERROR and 500.
`Log` prints key=value lines without timestamps; `Metrics` keeps counters in a sorted `TreeMap`.
One success, two rejections, one unknown room and one defect, each with its own status, log and counter.

pitfalls: Logging and rethrowing at every layer prints one failure three times and confuses incident timelines.
Catching only `RuntimeException` at the boundary turns every rejection into a 500 and pages on-call.
Matching on exception messages breaks the client when someone rewords the text; match on `code()`.

quiz.q: In ErrorBoundary, what does the third call return?
quiz.why: The slot check throws `InvalidSlotException` before the clash loop. The `BookingException` catch runs first, and the switch maps INVALID_SLOT to 400.

takeaway: Throw typed codes in the core; log, count and map once at the edge.
